title: More progress on the level editor for my game engine.
author: Sencha-Games
selftext:
I've since then added alt+click edge loop selection because I realized how much time was being wasted selecting edge loops. 

I'm aware of the brushes being slightly off-grid when I create them on projected geometry like near the end of the video. Working on resolving that.

And, just as a reminder for those who didn't see my previous post:

My game engine will be licensed under the Apache 2.0 license. My main motivation for working on the engine is to make games that I want and hope that other people might find use in my work, as well!

comments.author: Felfedezni
comments.body: Interesting choice. Why not just adapt an existing foss game engine like godot or bevy?

replies.author: Sencha-Games
replies.body:
I was using Godot for a bit, wasn't the biggest fan of the workflow. Sencha is extremely opinionated, not general purpose. I want an engine that speaks the language of the kinds of games I want to make.

Bevy is ECS which is what Sencha uses under the hood. It's also more of a framework than an engine. If I were starting over in Rust, I likely would use Bevy as a base, and build things like my world streaming, debug console, and editor around it. But as it is, I've struggled to learn Rust and it's hard for me to read, so I wouldn't be able to audit the quality of the code when using AI.
